1	# Epic 7 Context: Personal Summary Export
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users can request an AI-generated narrative summary plus a raw-data export for any date period from Meus Registros, and track its progress through to completion. The core guarantee is independence: the user's raw data must never be held hostage by the AI narrative step — it downloads as soon as it's ready regardless of whether the narrative is still generating, has failed, or was skipped, and a period with zero Entries is reported as a clear, non-crashing "nothing to export" state rather than an empty file or dead end. Realizes UJ-5 (a user exporting a multi-month summary before a personal check-in). Depends on Epic 4's timeline surface (export operates over the same Entry history and is launched from Meus Registros). The scope is job mechanism, file delivery, and failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly outside acceptance scope.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 7.1: Request a Period Export & Job Status Tracking
12	- Story 7.2: Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download
13	- Story 7.3: Empty-Period Handling
14	
15	## Requirements & Constraints
16	
17	- Requesting an export is synchronous-on-enqueue: the create call returns a `jobId` and an initial `pending` status immediately; all progress after that is observed by polling a status endpoint (no push/streaming for export).
18	- The job's own `status` and the AI narrative's `narrativeStatus` are reported independently by the status endpoint, together with an entry count, per-leg error codes, and an explicit "download available" flag — the UI must branch on both fields together, never infer one from the other.
19	- Five user-visible states cover every combination: preparing (no download), generating summary (no download), a hybrid "data ready, summary still generating" state (raw download already enabled while narrative keeps processing underneath — this combination is not one of the five states shown in the prototype itself but is required by the live contract), done-with-summary (both PDF and raw download), and done-or-error-with-narrative-only-failure (raw download only, error copy framed around the narrative, never around the whole job).
20	- An export requested over a period with zero Entries surfaces as its own terminal state ("Período vazio") — no download offered, no crash — and the copy should suggest adjusting the period/filter rather than leaving a dead end.
21	- The narrative step uses a hosted AI model server-side; the app never calls it directly and never grades or asserts on the generated text's content.
22	- Downloading a finished artifact (PDF or raw) resolves through a redirect to a signed storage URL, not a direct JSON payload.
23	- Every export error still carries the shared `{ code, message, retryable }` shape; `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` is non-retryable, so it is never fed into generic retry handling.
24	
25	## Technical Decisions
26	
27	- Export lives in its own feature slice, following the same layer direction and `Either<Failure, T>` repository boundary used everywhere else; it introduces no new error-signaling shape.
28	- The closed, shared `Failure` hierarchy already carries a dedicated case for the empty-period error; export must map onto that existing case rather than defining a feature-local error type.
29	- The job's progress (pending → processing → data-ready/done/error, with narrative status layered on top) is its own small sealed state class, not forced into the shared single-fetch `idle/loading/data/error` resource pattern — this mirrors how other multi-stage async flows (capture processing, chat streaming) in this codebase already get their own state machine rather than reusing the generic one.
30	- Retry behavior for the underlying HTTP calls is not reimplemented per feature — the shared API client already retries the handful of server codes marked retryable, and export's status/download calls follow that same single retry path rather than adding a second one.
31	- Calls are made by function name, never the literal REST path: export's three operations (create job, poll status, download) each resolve to their own named endpoint, with the job id appended as a trailing path segment where required.
32	- Prefer one export surface with an internal status enum over separate routes per stage — the underlying job has five+ states but is one continuously-updating surface, not five screens.
33	
34	## UX & Interaction Patterns
35	
36	- Entry point is a download icon in the Meus Registros header; it opens a bottom sheet — the heaviest sheet surface in the product short of a full-screen modal — using the same rise-from-bottom entrance timing as other sheets (skipped under Reduce Motion, final state shown immediately instead).
37	- Each stage transition replaces the sheet's content in place; the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job, and every state keeps a "Fechar" dismiss affordance.
38	- State copy is plain and factual, never celebratory: preparing shows a spinner ("Preparando exportação..."); generating shows a progress bar ("Gerando resumo com IA..."); the hybrid state shows the raw-data download already enabled with summary-progress text still visible underneath; full success shows a confirmation plus both download actions (PDF primary, raw data secondary); a narrative-only failure keeps just the raw-data action with error copy scoped to the narrative; the empty-period state shows explanatory copy and a suggestion to adjust the period, with no download action at all.
39	- No swipe gestures and no nested overlays — the export sheet sits alone on the scrim over Meus Registros, never stacking on another sheet.
40	
41	## Cross-Story Dependencies
42	
43	- Story 7.1 establishes the export request + status-polling state machine; Stories 7.2 and 7.3 are both refinements of states that machine must already be able to represent (the data-ready hybrid state, and the empty-period terminal state), not independent flows.
44	- The epic depends on Meus Registros (Epic 4) already existing as the launch surface and as the source of the period/filter the export is requested over.

# Epic 7 Context: Personal Summary Export

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can request an AI-generated narrative summary plus a raw-data export for any date period from Meus Registros, and track its progress through to completion. The core guarantee is independence: the user's raw data must never be held hostage by the AI narrative step — it downloads as soon as it's ready regardless of whether the narrative is still generating, has failed, or was skipped, and a period with zero Entries is reported as a clear, non-crashing "nothing to export" state rather than an empty file or dead end. Realizes UJ-5 (a user exporting a multi-month summary before a personal check-in). Depends on Epic 4's timeline surface (export operates over the same Entry history and is launched from Meus Registros). The scope is job mechanism, file delivery, and failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly outside acceptance scope.

## Stories

- Story 7.1: Request a Period Export & Job Status Tracking
- Story 7.2: Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download
- Story 7.3: Empty-Period Handling

## Requirements & Constraints

- Requesting an export is synchronous-on-enqueue: the create call returns a `jobId` and an initial `pending` status immediately; all progress after that is observed by polling a status endpoint (no push/streaming for export).
- The job's own `status` and the AI narrative's `narrativeStatus` are reported independently by the status endpoint, together with an entry count, per-leg error codes, and an explicit "download available" flag — the UI must branch on both fields together, never infer one from the other.
- Five user-visible states cover every combination: preparing (no download), generating summary (no download), a hybrid "data ready, summary still generating" state (raw download already enabled while narrative keeps processing underneath — this combination is not one of the five states shown in the prototype itself but is required by the live contract), done-with-summary (both PDF and raw download), and done-or-error-with-narrative-only-failure (raw download only, error copy framed around the narrative, never around the whole job).
- An export requested over a period with zero Entries surfaces as its own terminal state ("Período vazio") — no download offered, no crash — and the copy should suggest adjusting the period/filter rather than leaving a dead end.
- The narrative step uses a hosted AI model server-side; the app never calls it directly and never grades or asserts on the generated text's content.
- Downloading a finished artifact (PDF or raw) resolves through a redirect to a signed storage URL, not a direct JSON payload.
- Every export error still carries the shared `{ code, message, retryable }` shape; `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` is non-retryable, so it is never fed into generic retry handling.

## Technical Decisions

- Export lives in its own feature slice, following the same layer direction and `Either<Failure, T>` repository boundary used everywhere else; it introduces no new error-signaling shape.
- The closed, shared `Failure` hierarchy already carries a dedicated case for the empty-period error; export must map onto that existing case rather than defining a feature-local error type.
- The job's progress (pending → processing → data-ready/done/error, with narrative status layered on top) is its own small sealed state class, not forced into the shared single-fetch `idle/loading/data/error` resource pattern — this mirrors how other multi-stage async flows (capture processing, chat streaming) in this codebase already get their own state machine rather than reusing the generic one.
- Retry behavior for the underlying HTTP calls is not reimplemented per feature — the shared API client already retries the handful of server codes marked retryable, and export's status/download calls follow that same single retry path rather than adding a second one.
- Calls are made by function name, never the literal REST path: export's three operations (create job, poll status, download) each resolve to their own named endpoint, with the job id appended as a trailing path segment where required.
- Prefer one export surface with an internal status enum over separate routes per stage — the underlying job has five+ states but is one continuously-updating surface, not five screens.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Entry point is a download icon in the Meus Registros header; it opens a bottom sheet — the heaviest sheet surface in the product short of a full-screen modal — using the same rise-from-bottom entrance timing as other sheets (skipped under Reduce Motion, final state shown immediately instead).
- Each stage transition replaces the sheet's content in place; the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job, and every state keeps a "Fechar" dismiss affordance.
- State copy is plain and factual, never celebratory: preparing shows a spinner ("Preparando exportação..."); generating shows a progress bar ("Gerando resumo com IA..."); the hybrid state shows the raw-data download already enabled with summary-progress text still visible underneath; full success shows a confirmation plus both download actions (PDF primary, raw data secondary); a narrative-only failure keeps just the raw-data action with error copy scoped to the narrative; the empty-period state shows explanatory copy and a suggestion to adjust the period, with no download action at all.
- No swipe gestures and no nested overlays — the export sheet sits alone on the scrim over Meus Registros, never stacking on another sheet.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 7.1 establishes the export request + status-polling state machine; Stories 7.2 and 7.3 are both refinements of states that machine must already be able to represent (the data-ready hybrid state, and the empty-period terminal state), not independent flows.
- The epic depends on Meus Registros (Epic 4) already existing as the launch surface and as the source of the period/filter the export is requested over.

## Intent

**Problem:** Spec-7-1 left both download buttons `onPressed: null` and folded `data_ready` into the same visual as `processing` — raw data is never actually downloadable, even once the backend has it ready ahead of the narrative.

**Approach:** Wire `GET /export/:jobId/download` behind both buttons (open the signed URL externally, never buffer it in-app), and give `data_ready` its own state so the sheet shows "Baixar dados brutos" already enabled while the narrative keeps processing underneath.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `export-download-get` by function name, `jobId` trailing, `format=pdf|raw` query param.
- Capture the `302`'s `Location` header directly (`followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`) — never auto-follow into the signed-storage host.
- Open the signed URL externally (new `DownloadOpener` port, `url_launcher`-backed) — never buffer/write the file in-app.
- `data_ready` → its own `ExportJobState.dataReady()`: same progress-bar/text as `generating`, plus the now-enabled raw button beneath.
- A download failure shows an inline `SnackBar` (mirrors `_onExportTap`'s create-failure pattern), never mutates the sheet's job-status content.

**Ask First:** None — docs/input is silent on how a finished file reaches the user; external-open vs. in-app buffering is decided here.

**Never:** add a new `Failure` subtype for download errors (reuse `Failure.fromCode`, AD-3); touch empty-period state/copy (Story 7.3); add a busy state to `AppButton` itself (deferred).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Hybrid state | `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing` | Progress bar + text + enabled "Baixar dados brutos" | N/A |

| Missing `Location` | `302` with no header | `Failure.malformedResponse` | Same `SnackBar` path |

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- Download mechanism (docs/input silent): open the signed URL externally via `url_launcher` rather than buffering bytes in-app — no storage permissions, no local file/share-sheet plumbing.
- Download-tap failures surface via `SnackBar`, not a cubit state transition — the sealed `ExportJobState` models job *progress*, not one-off actions; a transient failure must never mutate the displayed state.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub add url_launcher` -- resolves cleanly
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- no conflicts
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- all pass

## Suggested Review Order

**Redirect-based download (entry point)**

- The one place a non-JSON, `302`-shaped response is handled: `followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`, error bodies still decode as JSON so existing error-mapping is untouched.
  [`api_client.dart:102`](../../lib/core/network/api_client.dart#L102)

**Download wiring through the layers**

- The port every other layer calls through — `jobId` + `format` in, signed URL out.
  [`export_repository.dart:41`](../../lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart#L41)

- Resolves to `export-download-get` by function name, `format.name` as the query value verbatim.
  [`export_remote_data_source.dart:85`](../../lib/features/export/data/datasources/export_remote_data_source.dart#L85)

- Thin pass-through, no cache — same shape as every other method on this repository.
  [`export_repository_impl.dart:34`](../../lib/features/export/data/repositories/export_repository_impl.dart#L34)

**The hybrid `data_ready` state**

- `data_ready` gets its own sealed case instead of folding into `generating` — the whole point of this story.
  [`export_job_state.dart:35`](../../lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart#L35)

- Where the DTO's raw `status` string is split into this new case.
  [`export_job_status_dto.dart:59`](../../lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart#L59)

**Cubit download lifecycle (review-patch round)**

- `_download`'s own shape after review: in-flight guard, `jobId == null` and a throwing opener both map to `Failure`, returned directly rather than through a shared field.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:161`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L161)

- The guard itself — a second call while one is in flight is a no-op, mirroring `_pollInFlight`.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:145`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L145)

- `downloadPdf`/`downloadRawData`'s own `Future<Failure?>` signature — what callers actually see.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:148`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L148)

- The domain port — never promises it won't throw, which is exactly why the cubit now guards its own call to it.
  [`download_opener.dart:11`](../../lib/features/export/domain/services/download_opener.dart#L11)

We're implementing Story 7.3 "Empty-Period Handling" in a Flutter app called Cerne (reflective journaling app, Clean Architecture, repo root /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b). This is the final story in Epic 7 (export feature). Stories 7.1 and 7.2 are already done: 7.1 built the export-request + job-status-polling state machine (ExportJobState sealed class), 7.2 wired up the actual download buttons and added a `dataReady` hybrid state.

Story 7.3's job: when a user requests an export over a date period with zero Entries, the UI must show its own terminal state ("Período vazio" — "Empty period") with no download action, explanatory copy suggesting the user adjust the period/filter, and no crash. This is reported via the backend's shared `{ code, message, retryable }` error shape with code `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, which is non-retryable and must map onto the *existing* `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod` case (NOT a new Failure subtype).

I need a distilled investigation report (not full file dumps — just exact findings with file:line anchors) covering:

1. **Backend contract**: Open `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` and find the export endpoints (create export job, get export status, download). Specifically: is `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` returned as an error on the *create* call (i.e., the POST to create a job fails outright when the period has zero entries), or does it show up as part of the status-polling response (e.g. a `status` or `error` field on the job-status GET)? Quote the exact schema/field names and where this code appears. Also check `docs/input/backend/README.md` for the function-name mapping of these endpoints, and check `docs/input/backend/` for any error-taxonomy doc that defines `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s exact shape and whether it's retryable (confirm the retryable value matches what's already in lib/core/failure/failure.dart). Also check for a file like `export-screen-states.md` (referenced in a prior spec's Code Map) — read it fully if it exists, it may define exact state semantics/copy for the empty-period state.

2. **Prototype**: Check `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` and `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` for any "Período vazio" or empty-period export state — exact copy text (Portuguese), any icon/visual treatment, button/affordance (just "Fechar"?).

3. **Requirements doc**: Open `docs/input/requirements.md` and find Story 7.3's exact acceptance criteria text (search for "7.3", "Empty-Period", "Período vazio", "EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD").

4. **Current code** — read and report exact current shape (with line numbers) of:
   - `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` — confirm the `ExportEmptyPeriod` case, its `retryable` mapping, and `Failure.fromCode`'s `'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD'` branch (already exists per a recent diff I saw — confirm exact current line numbers post-reformat).
   - `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart` — full current sealed-class shape (all states, especially `preparing`, `generating`, `dataReady`, `done`, `error` if any).
   - `lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart` — the `toState()` (or similar) mapping method, especially how it currently handles the create-call response and the status-poll response and whether/how it currently handles any error code at all.
   - `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` — how `_onExportTap`/create-job and polling currently handle a `Left(Failure)` from the repository (e.g. does create-job failure currently just show a SnackBar and leave sheet closed, or does it transition sheet state?).
   - `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart` — the `_contentFor` state-dispatch structure (so I know where a new case would plug in) and current empty/error-state handling if any already exists.
   - `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart` and its impl — the `createExportJob` (or equivalent) method signature, to see if it already returns `Either<Failure, T>` such that an empty-period failure would naturally flow through.
   - Any existing test file structure under `test/features/export/` relevant to error states (just note file paths, don't need full dumps).

Report back concisely: for each numbered area above, the key facts with file:line citations. Flag anything surprising (e.g. if EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD actually comes back from the status-poll endpoint rather than create, that changes the state-machine design significantly). Keep the report tight and factual — no implementation recommendations, just findings.

  INVESTIGATION REPORT — Story 7.3 "Empty-Period Handling"
  
  === 1. BACKEND CONTRACT ===
  
  `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`:
  
  - `POST /export/summary` (`operationId: export.summary.create`, `x-cerne-function: export-summary-create`), lines 1417-1476. Summary text: "Request export — synchronous count, enqueues the job" (line 1420). Success response is `'202'` returning only `{jobId, status: 'pending'}` (lines 1446-1470, `status` enum has exactly one value: `pending`). Error response is just `default: Error` → `$ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'` (lines 1471-1476) — the generic shared error shape, no endpoint-specific error enum.
  - `GET /export/{jobId}/status` (`export.status.get`, `export-status-get`), lines 1477-1550. `status` enum (line 1504-1511): `pending | processing | data_ready | done | error` — **no `empty_period`/dedicated value**. `errorCode` (lines 1524-1526) is a free `string, nullable: true` with **no enum restriction** at this endpoint (unlike the shared `Error.code` schema, which IS enum-restricted).
  - `GET /export/{jobId}/download` (`export.download.get`, `export-download-get`), lines 1551-1581. `'302'` redirect or generic `default: Error`.
  - Shared `components/schemas/Error` (lines 1875-1904): `{code (enum of the closed 13 codes, including `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` at line 1891), message, retryable, requestId}` — all four `required`.
  
  Finding to flag: `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` is only ever named explicitly in (a) the generic `Error.code` enum (reusable on *any* `default: Error` response, including the create call's), and (b) unrelated at line 1385 inside `/chat/sessions/{id}/insight`'s `errorCode` enum (a different feature's reflection-insight entity, not export). The contract text itself never pins `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` to either the create call or the status-poll response specifically — it's ambiguous by the OpenAPI schema alone which path actually returns it, because `/export/summary`'s only documented error path is the generic `default: Error` (so a synchronous-count rejection fits that shape), while `/export/{jobId}/status`'s own `errorCode` field being unenum'd free-text also leaves room for it there.
  
  `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md` (full file, 15 lines) — the explicit "Code Map" cross-reference doc for RF05: a 6-row table (Preparing/Generating/Data-ready/Done+summary/Done-summary-failed/Error), entirely driven by `status`/`narrativeStatus`/`downloadAvailable` from `GET /export/{jobId}/status`. **It has NO row for an empty-period/"Período vazio" state at all** — the "Export error" row (`status: error`, `narrativeStatus: —`, download: no) is the closest match, with no sub-breakdown by `errorCode`.
  
  `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` — closed 13-code table. `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD | 400 | retryable: no` (line 17). This matches `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`'s `retryable => false` for `ExportEmptyPeriod()` exactly.
  
  `docs/input/backend/README.md` lines 40-42 — function-name mapping: `POST /export/summary → export-summary-create`, `GET /export/{jobId}/status → export-status-get`, `GET /export/{jobId}/download → export-download-get`. Line 11 lists `export-screen-states.md` itself as "Mapping between the export screen states and the export job statuses (RF05)".
  
  === 2. PROTOTYPE ===
  
  `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`:
  - Line 32 (state catalog overview): `overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period`
  - Line 48: prototype's 32-state catalog names "Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio" as one of its named states.
  - Section 2.5 "Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)", lines 95-104:
    - Line 102: `| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |`
    - Line 104: "All five have the link **'Fechar'** at the bottom." No other button/affordance for the empty-period state besides "Fechar".
  
  `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` — minified; the only textual hit is a nav-menu entry (not sheet copy): `{ id: 'exp_empty', label: 'Exportar — Período vazio', rf: 'RF05', go: () => this.jump({ screen: 'registros', exportState: 'empty' }) }` — confirms a dedicated `exportState: 'empty'` jump target exists in the prototype's own routing, but no additional copy/icon beyond what prototype-extract.md already quotes.
  
  === 3. REQUIREMENTS DOC ===
  
  `docs/input/requirements.md` has no literal "7.3"/"Empty-Period Handling" string — that numbering lives only in the BMad planning artifacts (not requirements.md). Requirements.md's relevant acceptance criterion is under **RF05** (lines 37-42): "An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash)." (line 41).
  
  The actual Story 7.3 text (found in `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md` lines 918-932, and context doc `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-7-context.md`):
  - epics.md line 892: "the sheet reflects exactly five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — reporting `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently" (this is actually under **Story 7.1**'s AC, framed as arriving via `GET /export/:jobId/status` polling).
  - epics.md lines 918-932 (Story 7.3 itself): AC1 "Given I request an export for a period with zero Entries / When the job resolves / Then `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` surfaces as 'Período vazio' with no download button offered and no crash." AC2: "Given this error state / When I view it / Then it suggests adjusting the filter/period rather than leaving me with a dead end."
  - epic-7-context.md line 20/38/43: reiterates "empty-period terminal state," non-retryable, must map onto the existing `Failure` case, and that 7.3 is "a refinement of a state the [7.1] machine must already be able to represent... not an independent flow."
  
  **Flag**: these planning docs consistently frame `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` as something discovered through **status polling** ("when the job resolves," "poll via status"), which is in tension with the OpenAPI contract's `/export/summary` create-call summary text "synchronous count" and its generic `default: Error` response shape (section 1) — the planning docs do not address the create-call path at all.
  
  === 4. CURRENT CODE ===
  
  **`lib/core/failure/failure.dart`**: `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) = ExportEmptyPeriod` at lines 30-31. `retryable` getter's `false`-branch includes `ExportEmptyPeriod()` at line 56. `Failure.fromCode`'s `'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message)` branch at line 77. All already present and correct — not something to add.
  
  **`lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart`** — sealed class already has **6** states, not 5: `preparing` (19-23), `generating` (25-27), `dataReady` (29-35, added in 7.2), `done(ExportOutcome outcome)` (37-42, outcome enum `narrativeReady`/`narrativeUnavailable`, lines 109-118), `error(Failure failure)` (44-48), and **`emptyPeriod()` (50-60, class `ExportJobEmptyPeriod` at lines 161-172)** — already fully defined, no-arg, with `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`. This was added in commit `753d448` (Story 7.1), confirmed via `git log -p`.
  
  **`lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart`** — `toState()` method (lines 53-86): `'pending'→preparing`, `'processing'→generating`, `'data_ready'→dataReady`, `'done'→done(outcome from narrativeStatus)`, `'error'→` builds `Failure.fromCode(errorCode ?? '', ...)` then branches: `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod ? ExportJobState.emptyPeriod() : ExportJobState.error(failure)` (lines 71-77) — **this is exactly the AD-3-compliant mapping Story 7.3 asks for, and it already exists**, scoped to the status-poll response only. `default:` branch → `ExportJobState.error(Failure.malformedResponse(...))` for an unrecognized `status` string (lines 78-84). There is no handling of any error code on the create-call response in this file (DTO only models the status-poll shape).
  
  **`lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart`** — `start()` (lines 65-87): on `Left(failure)` from `_repository.createJob(...)`, **always** does `emit(ExportJobState.error(failure)); return false;` (lines 77-80) regardless of which `Failure` subtype — **no `is ExportEmptyPeriod` branch exists on the create path**, unlike the DTO's poll-path handling. `_poll()` (lines 94-130): on `Right(newState)` from `getStatus`, just `emit(newState)` (line 121) — relies entirely on the DTO's `toState()` having already produced `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`. `_isTerminal()` (lines 132-135) already includes `state is ExportJobEmptyPeriod` alongside `ExportJobDone`/`ExportJobError` — so once emitted, polling correctly stops.
  
  **`lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart`** — `_contentFor` switch (lines 158-203) already has an `ExportJobEmptyPeriod() => [...]` case (lines 195-202) rendering exactly the prototype copy: `_StatusText('Nenhum registro nesse período.')` then `_StatusText('Ajuste o filtro de período e tente de novo.', color: colorTextSecondary)` — no download button, and the sheet's single shared "Fechar" link (lines 120-127, outside the switch) is the only affordance, matching prototype-extract.md line 104.
  
  **`lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart`**: `createJob(...) → Future<Either<Failure, String>>` (line 18-21, doc comment explicitly says "every `Failure` here, including a theoretical synchronous rejection, propagates as `Left`, unmapped" — line 17), `getStatus(jobId) → Future<Either<Failure, ExportJobState>>` (line 31, doc states "a backend-reported job failure (including the empty-period case) already arrives as a `Right(ExportJobState.error(...))`/`Right(ExportJobState.emptyPeriod())`, never as a `Left`" — lines 27-30), `getDownloadUrl(...)`. Impl (`export_repository_impl.dart`) is a thin pass-through; `getStatus` does `result.map((dto) => dto.toState())` (line 30) — all mapping logic lives in the DTO, none in the repo/impl.
  
  `lib/features/export/data/datasources/export_remote_data_source.dart`: `createJob` (lines 30-63) posts to `export-summary-create` and only catches decode exceptions into `malformedResponse` (lines 55-61) — any `Left` from `_apiClient.post` itself (HTTP-level error, including a hypothetical 400 `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` on create) passes straight through unmodified. `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart` lines 259, 307) already builds these via `Failure.fromCode`, so a create-call 400 with `code: EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` would already decode to `Left(Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(...))` — but the cubit's `start()` (above) does not special-case it, so it would currently surface as the generic `ExportJobError` sheet state/copy ("Não foi possível gerar a exportação."), not "Período vazio".
  
  **Tests** under `test/features/export/`:
  - `data/datasources/export_remote_data_source_test.dart`
  - `data/models/export_job_status_dto_test.dart` — line 68-75: `'error' + errorCode EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD -> emptyPeriod, never a plain error(Failure)'` already covers the DTO mapping.
  - `data/services/url_launcher_download_opener_test.dart`
  - `export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — lines 327-350: `'Período vazio: status error with errorCode EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD maps end-to-end ... pipeline to ExportJobState.emptyPeriod(), not a generic error'` — full repo→cubit e2e test, status-poll path only.
  - `presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart` — line 302-313: `'Período vazio: emptyPeriod is terminal — polling stops...'` (status-poll path). Line 171-194: `'Create fails: emits error...'` test exists but uses `Failure.networkOffline`, **not** `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod` — no test exercises an `ExportEmptyPeriod` `Left` from `createJob`.
  - `presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet_test.dart` — line 355-358+: `'Período vazio: adjust-period copy, no download button offered'` widget test, feeding `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` directly via `getStatusResults`.
  
  === KEY FLAG ===
  
  Everything needed for Story 7.3 **already exists and is already tested**, but exclusively on the **status-poll path** (`GET /export/{jobId}/status` → DTO `toState()` → `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` → cubit `_isTerminal` → sheet copy) — this was built as part of Story 7.1's commit (`753d448`), not freshly for 7.3. The one path with **no** empty-period handling and **no** test coverage is the **create-call path**: `ExportJobCubit.start()` (lines 76-80) emits a generic `ExportJobState.error(failure)` for *any* `Left` from `createJob`, with no `is ExportEmptyPeriod` branch — so if the backend actually rejects `POST /export/summary` synchronously with `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` (which its OpenAPI summary text "synchronous count, enqueues the job" suggests is plausible, and which the generic `default: Error` ref on that endpoint technically allows per the shared, enum-restricted `Error.code` schema), the user would currently see the generic "Não foi possível gerar a exportação." error copy instead of "Nenhum registro nesse período." + adjust-period suggestion. The backend's own `export-screen-states.md` Code Map doc, by contrast, has no empty-period row in its table at all and frames everything purely in terms of the status-poll `status`/`narrativeStatus`/`downloadAvailable` combination — consistent with the existing code's design choice to treat empty-period exclusively as a status-poll outcome, but this is not something the OpenAPI schema itself rules out happening on create instead/also.
  
</agent-message>

7	/// sites read as `ExportJobState.preparing()` rather than naming each
8	/// subclass directly. Exactly the 6 states `docs/input/backend/export-
9	/// screen-states.md`'s own status×narrativeStatus×downloadAvailable table

12	/// wire.

14	/// Never persisted (AD-15: ephemeral, polled live) — lives only on
15	/// `ExportJobCubit.state`.
16	sealed class ExportJobState {
17	  const ExportJobState();

34	  /// the narrative in, which isn't done yet).

38	  /// succeeded, both download buttons shown) from "Narrativa falhou/
39	  /// pulada" (only the raw-data button, copy scoped to the narrative
40	  /// failure) without needing two separate sealed variants for what is,
41	  /// to the job itself, one and the same terminal success.
42	  const factory ExportJobState.done(ExportOutcome outcome) = ExportJobDone;

---
title: 'Empty-Period Handling'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-07'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '3ce4d329a1943d6ebfeae891e5dc3adc9097943b'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `export-summary-create`'s own OpenAPI summary — "synchronous count, enqueues the job" — plus `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400`/non-retryable entry in `error-taxonomy.md` mean the backend rejects the *create* call itself, synchronously, for a zero-Entry period — it never gets a `jobId`. `ExportJobCubit.start()` doesn't special-case this: every create failure, `ExportEmptyPeriod` included, emits the generic `ExportJobState.error(failure)` and returns `false`, which `MeusRegistrosScreen._onExportTap()` reads as "never open the sheet — inline `SnackBar` instead." The user would see the generic "Não foi possível gerar a exportação." SnackBar, not the prototype's dedicated "Período vazio" sheet state.

**Approach:** In `start()`'s create-failure branch, special-case `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod`: emit `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (already exists, built for the poll path in Story 7.1) and return `true` instead of `false` — the screen's existing `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` then opens the sheet unchanged, landing directly on the already-correct "Período vazio" content. No `jobId` is stored and polling never starts.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Only functional change: `ExportJobCubit.start()`'s create-failure handler. No change to `ExportJobState`, `ExportJobStatusDto`, `ExportStatusSheet`, or `MeusRegistrosScreen`.
- On this branch, `_jobId` stays `null` and `_startPolling()` is never called — there is no job to poll.
- Reuse `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod`/`ExportEmptyPeriod` (AD-3) via an `is` check — never a new `Failure` subtype, never a string check on `failure.message`.
- Every other create-failure subtype keeps today's exact behavior: `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false`, sheet never opens.

**Ask First:** None — the contract (create endpoint's "synchronous count" summary + `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400` entry) is specific enough to settle the delivery path without a human call.

**Never:** touch the DTO's existing poll-path `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` → `emptyPeriod()` mapping (`export_job_status_dto.dart`) — leave it as defensive coverage in case the backend ever also reports it there; touch `ExportStatusSheet._contentFor`'s empty-period copy/layout (already matches the prototype exactly); add a new `Failure` subtype or new `ExportJobState` variant.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
| Create rejected, empty period | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(...))` | `start()` emits `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`, returns `true`; sheet opens on "Período vazio" | N/A |
| Create rejected, other failure | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.networkOffline(...))` (unchanged) | emits `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false` | inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens (existing, untouched) |
| Empty-period terminal, no poll | After the above | `_jobId` stays `null`; elapsing time never triggers `getStatus` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart:76-80` -- `start()`'s `result.match` failure branch: add the `is ExportEmptyPeriod` check described in Approach. The only line-level change in this spec.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:30-31` -- `ExportEmptyPeriod` case (already exists, Story 7.1) -- read-only, used for the `is` check.
- `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart:60,161-172` -- `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`/`ExportJobEmptyPeriod` (already exists) -- read-only, emitted as-is.
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:196-241` -- `_onExportTap` -- read-only; its existing `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` already does the right thing once `start()` returns `true` for this case. Confirm no change needed.
- `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart:195-202` -- `ExportJobEmptyPeriod()` case in `_contentFor` (already exists) -- read-only, renders unchanged.
- `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart:171-194` -- sibling test to the existing "Create fails: emits error..." test, for the new branch.
- `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart:326-350` -- sibling test to the existing poll-path "Período vazio" e2e test, for the create-path.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` -- branch `start()`'s create-failure handler on `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod` -- closes the one path (contract: `export-summary-create`'s synchronous rejection) not already covered by Story 7.1's poll-path handling in the DTO.
- [ ] `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart` -- unit test: `createJobResult = left(const Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: ...))` → `started` is `true`, `cubit.state` is `ExportJobEmptyPeriod`, elapsing a poll interval never calls `getStatus`.
- [ ] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` -- e2e test: queue a single `400` response `{'code': 'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD', 'message': ..., 'retryable': false}` to `export-summary-create`, drive the real `ExportJobCubit` through DI, assert `cubit.state is ExportJobEmptyPeriod` and that `export-status-get` is never requested.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a period with zero Entries, when the user requests an export and `export-summary-create` rejects synchronously with `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, then the sheet opens directly into "Período vazio" (no download button, "Fechar" only) — never a generic error `SnackBar`, never a crash.
- Given that empty-period state, then no poll ever fires — there was never a `jobId` to poll.
- Given a different create failure (any other `Failure` subtype), then today's existing behavior is unchanged: inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens.

## Design Notes

`start()` returning `true` for this one failure case is deliberate, not an oversight: from the screen's point of view, reaching a valid terminal UI state (the sheet showing "Período vazio") is success, even though no job was actually created. This is the one place `start()`'s boolean return stops meaning "job created" and starts meaning "safe to open the sheet" — the same reinterpretation the empty-period AC already forces on the sheet itself (a sheet state with no underlying job).

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/features/export/` -- all pass, including the two new tests

---
title: 'Empty-Period Handling'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-07'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '3ce4d329a1943d6ebfeae891e5dc3adc9097943b'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `export-summary-create`'s own OpenAPI summary — "synchronous count, enqueues the job" — plus `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400`/non-retryable entry in `error-taxonomy.md` mean the backend rejects the *create* call itself, synchronously, for a zero-Entry period — it never gets a `jobId`. `ExportJobCubit.start()` doesn't special-case this: every create failure, `ExportEmptyPeriod` included, emits the generic `ExportJobState.error(failure)` and returns `false`, which `MeusRegistrosScreen._onExportTap()` reads as "never open the sheet — inline `SnackBar` instead." The user would see the generic "Não foi possível gerar a exportação." SnackBar, not the prototype's dedicated "Período vazio" sheet state.

**Approach:** In `start()`'s create-failure branch, special-case `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod`: emit `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (already exists, built for the poll path in Story 7.1) and return `true` instead of `false` — the screen's existing `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` then opens the sheet unchanged, landing directly on the already-correct "Período vazio" content. No `jobId` is stored and polling never starts.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Only functional change: `ExportJobCubit.start()`'s create-failure handler. No change to `ExportJobState`, `ExportJobStatusDto`, `ExportStatusSheet`, or `MeusRegistrosScreen`.
- On this branch, `_jobId` stays `null`, `_startPolling()` is never called.
- Reuse `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod`/`ExportEmptyPeriod` (AD-3) via an `is` check — never a new `Failure` subtype or a string check on `failure.message`.
- Every other create-failure subtype keeps today's behavior: `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false`, sheet never opens.

**Ask First:** None — the contract (create endpoint's "synchronous count" summary + `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400` entry) is specific enough to settle the delivery path without a human call.

**Never:** touch the DTO's existing poll-path `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` → `emptyPeriod()` mapping (`export_job_status_dto.dart`) — leave it as defensive coverage in case the backend ever also reports it there; touch `ExportStatusSheet._contentFor`'s empty-period copy/layout (already matches the prototype exactly); add a new `Failure` subtype or new `ExportJobState` variant.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
| Create rejected, empty period | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(...))` | `start()` emits `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`, returns `true`; sheet opens on "Período vazio" | N/A |
| Create rejected, other failure | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.networkOffline(...))` (unchanged) | emits `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false` | inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens (existing, untouched) |
| Empty-period terminal, no poll | After the above | `_jobId` stays `null`; elapsing time never triggers `getStatus` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart:76-80` -- `start()`'s `result.match` failure branch -- add the `is ExportEmptyPeriod` check (Approach). Only line-level change in this spec.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:30-31` -- `ExportEmptyPeriod` (exists, Story 7.1) -- read-only, used for the `is` check.
- `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart:60,161-172` -- `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (exists) -- read-only, emitted as-is.
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:196-241` -- `_onExportTap` -- read-only; its `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` already opens the sheet once `start()` returns `true`.
- `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart:195-202` -- `ExportJobEmptyPeriod()` render case (exists) -- read-only.
- `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart:171-194` -- sibling to the existing "Create fails" test, for the new branch.
- `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart:326-350` -- sibling to the existing poll-path "Período vazio" e2e test, for the create-path.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` -- branch `start()`'s create-failure handler on `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod` -- closes the one path (contract: `export-summary-create`'s synchronous rejection) not already covered by Story 7.1's poll-path handling in the DTO.
- [ ] `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart` -- unit test: `createJobResult = left(const Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: ...))` → `started` is `true`, `cubit.state` is `ExportJobEmptyPeriod`, elapsing a poll interval never calls `getStatus`.
- [ ] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` -- e2e test: queue a single `400` response `{'code': 'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD', 'message': ..., 'retryable': false}` to `export-summary-create`, drive the real `ExportJobCubit` through DI, assert `cubit.state is ExportJobEmptyPeriod` and that `export-status-get` is never requested.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a period with zero Entries, when the user requests an export and `export-summary-create` rejects synchronously with `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, then the sheet opens directly into "Período vazio" (no download button, "Fechar" only) — never a generic error `SnackBar`, never a crash.
- Given that empty-period state, then no poll ever fires — there was never a `jobId` to poll.
- Given a different create failure (any other `Failure` subtype), then today's existing behavior is unchanged: inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens.

## Design Notes

`start()` returning `true` here is deliberate: for this one case its boolean stops meaning "job created" and starts meaning "safe to open the sheet" — the sheet shows "Período vazio" with no underlying job, mirroring what the empty-period AC already forces on the sheet itself.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/features/export/` -- all pass, including the two new tests

# Sync Sprint Status

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

## Instructions

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

---
title: 'Empty-Period Handling'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-07'

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `export-summary-create`'s summary — "synchronous count, enqueues the job" — plus `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400`/non-retryable entry in `error-taxonomy.md` mean the backend rejects the *create* call itself for a zero-Entry period, never issuing a `jobId`. `ExportJobCubit.start()` doesn't special-case this: every create failure emits the generic `ExportJobState.error(failure)` and returns `false`, which `MeusRegistrosScreen._onExportTap()` reads as "never open the sheet, show an inline `SnackBar` instead." The user sees "Não foi possível gerar a exportação.", not the prototype's "Período vazio" sheet state.

**Approach:** In `start()`'s create-failure branch, special-case `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod`: emit `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (already exists, built for the poll path in Story 7.1) and return `true` instead of `false` — the screen's existing `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` then opens the sheet unchanged, landing directly on the already-correct "Período vazio" content. No `jobId` is stored and polling never starts.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Only functional change: `ExportJobCubit.start()`'s create-failure handler. No change to `ExportJobState`, `ExportJobStatusDto`, `ExportStatusSheet`, or `MeusRegistrosScreen`.
- On this branch, `_jobId` stays `null`, `_startPolling()` is never called.
- Reuse `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod`/`ExportEmptyPeriod` (AD-3) via an `is` check — never a new `Failure` subtype or a string check on `failure.message`.
- Every other create-failure subtype keeps today's behavior: `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false`, sheet never opens.

**Ask First:** None — the contract (create endpoint's "synchronous count" summary + `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400` entry) is specific enough to settle the delivery path without a human call.

**Never:** touch the DTO's existing poll-path `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` → `emptyPeriod()` mapping (`export_job_status_dto.dart`) — leave it as defensive coverage in case the backend ever also reports it there; touch `ExportStatusSheet._contentFor`'s empty-period copy/layout (already matches the prototype exactly); add a new `Failure` subtype or new `ExportJobState` variant.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42	
43	### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test
44	
45	For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.
46	
47	A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.
48	
49	Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.
50	
51	- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
52	- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
53	- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.
54	
55	A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.
56	
57	For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.
58	
59	Common patterns:
60	
61	- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
62	- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
63	- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
64	- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
65	- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
66	- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.
67	
68	### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real
69	
70	Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.
71	
72	Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.
73	
74	Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.
75	
76	Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.
77	
78	## OUTPUT FORMAT
79	
80	Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.
81	
82	```markdown
83	### <one-line title naming the gap>
84	
85	- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
86	- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
87	- **Existing test evidence:**
88	  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
89	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
90	  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
91	- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
92	- **Demonstration:**
93	  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
94	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
95	- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
96	- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
97	```
98	
99	If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:
100	
101	```markdown
102	## Other findings
103	
104	- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
105	```
106	
107	When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:
108	
109	`No verification gaps found.`
110	
111	## CONTENT SOURCE
112	
113	Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`
114

- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

## Suggested Review Order

**{Concern name}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:42`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L42)

- {one-line framing}
  [`other.ts:17`](../../src/path/to/other.ts#L17)

**{Next concern}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:88`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L88)

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `export-summary-create`'s summary — "synchronous count, enqueues the job" — plus `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400`/non-retryable entry in `error-taxonomy.md` mean the backend rejects the *create* call itself for a zero-Entry period, never issuing a `jobId`. `ExportJobCubit.start()` doesn't special-case this: every create failure emits the generic `ExportJobState.error(failure)` and returns `false`, which `MeusRegistrosScreen._onExportTap()` reads as "never open the sheet, show an inline `SnackBar` instead." The user sees "Não foi possível gerar a exportação.", not the prototype's "Período vazio" sheet state.

**Approach:** In `start()`'s create-failure branch, special-case `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod`: emit `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (already exists, built for the poll path in Story 7.1) and return `true` instead of `false` — the screen's existing `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` then opens the sheet unchanged, landing directly on the already-correct "Período vazio" content. No `jobId` is stored and polling never starts.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Only functional change: `ExportJobCubit.start()`'s create-failure handler. No change to `ExportJobState`, `ExportJobStatusDto`, `ExportStatusSheet`, or `MeusRegistrosScreen`.
- On this branch, `_jobId` stays `null`, `_startPolling()` is never called.
- Reuse `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod`/`ExportEmptyPeriod` (AD-3) via an `is` check — never a new `Failure` subtype or a string check on `failure.message`.
- Every other create-failure subtype keeps today's behavior: `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false`, sheet never opens.

**Ask First:** None — the contract (create endpoint's "synchronous count" summary + `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s `400` entry) is specific enough to settle the delivery path without a human call.

**Never:** touch the DTO's existing poll-path `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` → `emptyPeriod()` mapping (`export_job_status_dto.dart`) — leave it as defensive coverage in case the backend ever also reports it there; touch `ExportStatusSheet._contentFor`'s empty-period copy/layout (already matches the prototype exactly); add a new `Failure` subtype or new `ExportJobState` variant.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
| Create rejected, empty period | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(...))` | `start()` emits `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`, returns `true`; sheet opens on "Período vazio" | N/A |
| Create rejected, other failure | `createJob` → `Left(Failure.networkOffline(...))` (unchanged) | emits `ExportJobState.error(failure)`, returns `false` | inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens (existing, untouched) |
| Empty-period terminal, no poll | After the above | `_jobId` stays `null`; elapsing time never triggers `getStatus` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart:76-80` -- `start()`'s `result.match` failure branch -- add the `is ExportEmptyPeriod` check (Approach). Only line-level change in this spec.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:30-31` -- `ExportEmptyPeriod` (exists, Story 7.1) -- read-only, used for the `is` check.
- `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart:60,161-172` -- `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` (exists) -- read-only, emitted as-is.
- `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:196-241` -- `_onExportTap` -- read-only; its `if (started) { ExportStatusSheet.show(...) }` already opens the sheet once `start()` returns `true`.
- `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart:195-202` -- `ExportJobEmptyPeriod()` render case (exists) -- read-only.
- `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart:171-194` -- sibling to the existing "Create fails" test, for the new branch.
- `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart:326-350` -- sibling to the existing poll-path "Período vazio" e2e test, for the create-path.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` -- branch `start()`'s create-failure handler on `failure is ExportEmptyPeriod` -- closes the one path (contract: `export-summary-create`'s synchronous rejection) not already covered by Story 7.1's poll-path handling in the DTO.
- [x] `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart` -- unit test: `createJobResult = left(const Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: ...))` → `started` is `true`, `cubit.state` is `ExportJobEmptyPeriod`, elapsing a poll interval never calls `getStatus`.
- [x] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` -- e2e test: queue a single `400` response `{'code': 'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD', 'message': ..., 'retryable': false}` to `export-summary-create`, drive the real `ExportJobCubit` through DI, assert `cubit.state is ExportJobEmptyPeriod` and that `export-status-get` is never requested.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a period with zero Entries, when the user requests an export and `export-summary-create` rejects synchronously with `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, then the sheet opens directly into "Período vazio" (no download button, "Fechar" only) — never a generic error `SnackBar`, never a crash.
- Given that empty-period state, then no poll ever fires — there was never a `jobId` to poll.
- Given a different create failure (any other `Failure` subtype), then today's existing behavior is unchanged: inline `SnackBar`, sheet never opens.

`start()` returning `true` here is deliberate: for this one case its boolean stops meaning "job created" and starts meaning "safe to open the sheet" — the sheet shows "Período vazio" with no underlying job, mirroring what the empty-period AC already forces on the sheet itself.

content.text:
## Summary

Story 7.3 (Empty-Period Handling) is implemented, reviewed, and committed.

**What it does:** `export-summary-create` rejects a zero-Entry period synchronously (400 `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, never issuing a `jobId`). `ExportJobCubit.start()` now special-cases that failure to emit `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()` and return `true` instead of the generic error path, so the export sheet opens directly on "Período vazio" instead of a generic SnackBar. The status-poll path for the same error code already existed from story 7.1 and was untouched.

**Review caught one real gap:** the initial implementation only fixed the cubit/e2e layers — nothing verified the actual screen-level hand-off through `MeusRegistrosScreen`/`ExportStatusSheet`. A widget test was added to close that, plus three stale doc comments were updated and a pointless 3-second real-wait was trimmed from the new e2e test.

**Commits:**
- `948fbed` — finishes off story 7.2's own outstanding, previously-uncommitted review-round fixes (kept separate so the history stays accurate)
- `7b79c31` — story 7.3's clean, isolated diff

The spec file was sent to VS Code — [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-7-3-empty-period-handling.md](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-7-3-empty-period-handling.md) contains a **Suggested Review Order**. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) the links in it to jump to each stop.

Left untouched, as before: ~71 unrelated pre-existing dirty files (pure `dart format`-style reformatting noise across other features) — not part of this story, left exactly as found.
